To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Graphiti allows users to specify network edges based on a set of nodes and links that they wish to see and that it recommends attribute-based linking conditions to users based on the demonstrated subset of nodes and edges.

1) users can model networks by demonstrating to the system a set of nodes and links, 2) the system can recommend linking conditions based on the demonstration, and 3) the system can also recommend additional edge types to be added to an existing network based on the demonstration.
Graphiti allows users to specify networks by showing the system a subset nodes and links and that Graphiti allows them to update existing networks by showing the same.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a novel approach for modeling networks by allowing users to demonstrate a subset of nodes they wish to see, along with a set of links between them.
the design and implementation of a novel interaction technique to model network visualizations.
the problem of interactive specification of attribute-based edges for network modeling and visualization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we present an interactive approach for network modeling that allows users to visualize and explore networks in a more natural way than existing approaches.
Graphiti provides users with an interactive and easy way to model networks from tabular data.
Graphiti is a novel tool for interactive modeling and visualization of network graphs that allows users to specify attribute-based linking conditions for edges in a network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an interaction technique that can be used for both modeling and visualization of networks.
Graphiti is a novel tool for network visualization and modeling that allows users to specify attribute-based linking conditions in an interactive manner.
Graphiti allows users to interactively specify attribute-based edge conditions for modeling networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a user demonstration-based interaction technique, coupled with a recommendation mechanism, can be used to facilitate the modeling of networks.
users can use Graphiti to model network visualizations from a tabular data source, without having to know the conditions to define edges.
by allowing users to interact with networks in an intuitive manner, we enable them to model networks from raw data without the burden of writing complex SQL commands or programming scripts.
